                    ### Question
                    A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for the past 3 days. He has also had 4 episodes of right-sided headaches over the past month. He has no significant past medical history. His father died of coronary artery disease at the age of 62 years. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 232/128 mm Hg. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered?

Immediate treatment is necessary to prevent further complications such as stroke. Nitroprusside is a rapid-acting antihypertensive commonly used in acute settings for its ability to quickly lower blood pressure, which aligns with the observed decrease to 190/105 mm Hg after administration. While Labetalol is also effective for acute hypertension, Nitroprusside is preferred for its rapid onset in emergencies. Other options like Hydralazine are less commonly used for immediate management in this context. Therefore, the most likely drug administered is Nitroprusside, supported by the consensus on its use in hypertensive emergencies.
